summary: Registers and documents the MIME types associated with the 3GPP2 multimedia file format, which belongs to the family based on the ISO Media File Format. It is standards-track.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 4393 registers the labels for media files used by third-generation mobile phones. It defines audio/3gpp2, for a file that holds only sound, and video/3gpp2, which may be used for any such file. A file that is given either label must say inside itself which specifications it follows, so a player can tell whether it should play the file.

questions: what file extension do 3gpp2 files use
subtitle: Registers audio/3gpp2 and video/3gpp2 so 3G2 phone media files can be labeled correctly over HTTP and in multipart documents.

tldr.problem: Files in the 3GPP2 multimedia format had no registered media type, so a server had no agreed label to put on them.
tldr.mechanism: The document registers two media types, audio/3gpp2 for files with sound and no pictures, and video/3gpp2 for any file, and specifies that such a file must carry a 3GPP2 brand in the list of brands it is compatible with.
tldr.outcome: A 3G2 file can now be served and attached with a type that says what it holds. RFC 4393 was later updated by RFC 6381.

today: RFC 4393 was published in March 2006 as a Proposed Standard and has since been updated by RFC 6381. The registrations remain the standard labels for 3GPP2 media files.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The third-generation partnership project 2, for 3rd generation cellular telephony, has defined a standard file format to contain audio and visual sequences that may be downloaded to cellular phones. At the time of writing, the 3GPP2 file format, called 3G2, can contain H.263, H.264 or MPEG-4 video, 13K Vocoder, EVRC or AMR narrow-band speech or AAC audio, and 3GPP timed text.

Within the file, as with all files in the ISO family, there is an intrinsic file-type box, which identifies those specifications to which the file complies, and which players, possibly compliant with only one specification, are permitted by the content author to play the file. This identification is through four-letter brands. Files identified by the MIME type defined in this document MUST contain, in their compatible brands list, a brand defined in a standard issued by 3GPP2 that can apply to 3GPP2 files.

The MIME types defined in this document are needed correctly to identify such files when they are served over HTTP, included in multi-part documents, or used in other places where MIME types are used.
sections.plainLanguage: Each 3G2 file lists the standards it follows, using short four-letter brand names, so that a player knows what it is allowed to do with it. The media type must not be used on a file that lacks a 3GPP2 brand.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The 3GPP2 file format may contain audio, video and displayable text data. There is currently no provision for active elements such as scripts of any kind.

Clearly, it is possible to author malicious files that attempt to call for an excessively large picture size, high sampling-rate audio, and so on. However, clients can and usually do protect themselves against this kind of attack.

It should be noted that selected metadata fields may encompass information partly intended to protect the media against unauthorized use or distribution. In this case, the intention is that alteration or removal of the data in the field would be treated as an offense under national agreement-based World Intellectual Property Organization treaties.

3GPP2 files have an extensible structure, so it is theoretically possible that metadata fields or media formats could be defined in the future that could be used to induce particular actions on the part of the recipient, thus presenting additional security risks. This type of capability is currently not supported in the referenced specification.

Encryption, signing or authentication of these file formats can be done using any media-independent transformations of the file or media data.
sections.plainLanguage: There is nothing active in the format, so the risk is a file that asks for far more picture or sound than the device can handle. Players normally defend against that. Signing or encrypting the file is left to whatever mechanism the surrounding system uses.

sections.title: The MIME Type Registration
sections.content:
The registration applies to all files defined as using the 3G2 file format and identified with a suitable brand in a 3GPP2 specification. The usual file suffix for all these files is .3g2.

Both registrations share the same details. There are no required parameters. The optional parameter Codecs follows the bucket media types; if the body part contains another container format, the Codecs parameter MUST list all codecs indicated by all formats, including any contained formats. The optional parameter value is [3gpp2].

For encoding, the data is binary and should be transmitted in a suitable encoding without CR/LF conversion or 7-bit stripping, and base64 is a suitable encoding. The MIME types are used only for files; separate types are used for real-time transfer, such as the RTP payload format for 13K vocoder speech and the RTP payload formats for H.263.

For interoperability, the 3GPP2 organization has defined the specification of the media format, and interoperability and conformance testing is done in cooperation with other bodies, including the Open Mobile Alliance and the International Multimedia Telecommunications Consortium. The published specifications are 3GPP2 C.S0045 and 3GPP2 C.S0050. The application is Multi-media. There is no magic number, but the file-type box must occur first in the file and MUST contain a 3GPP2 brand in its compatible brands list. The file extensions 3g2 and 3gpp2 are both declared, and 3g2 is preferred. The Macintosh file type code is 3gp2. The intended usage is COMMON and the change controller is 3GPP2.
sections.plainLanguage: The two types share their settings: one optional parameter listing the codecs, base64 for text transport, no magic number, and the usual file extension.

sections.title: Files with Audio but No Video
sections.content:
The type audio/3gpp2 may be used for files containing audio but no visual presentation, neither video nor timed text, for example.

The additional information in the registration states that the type audio/3gpp2 MAY be used for files containing audio but no visual presentation, and that files served under this type MUST NOT contain any visual material. It notes that 3GPP timed text is visually presented and is considered visual material.
sections.plainLanguage: Use the audio label only when there is nothing to see. Timed text counts as something to see, so a file with captions is not an audio-only file.

sections.title: Any Files
sections.content:
The type video/3gpp2 is valid for all files. It is valid to serve an audio-only file as video/3gpp2.

The registration repeats the shared details: no required parameters, the optional Codecs parameter that must list all codecs indicated by all formats when the body part contains another container format, binary encoding with base64 as a suitable encoding, no magic number but a file-type box that must occur first and must contain a 3GPP2 brand, the file extensions 3g2 and 3gpp2 with 3g2 preferred, the Macintosh file type code 3gp2, intended usage COMMON and change controller 3GPP2.
sections.plainLanguage: The video label works for anything, so a server can use it without inspecting the file. It is always safe to use, though it does not tell a client more than the file itself does.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content: This document registers the MIME media types audio/3gpp2 and video/3gpp2, defined above.
sections.plainLanguage: Two registrations, and that is all the document adds to the registry.

cells: For files with audio and no visual presentation

items.title: File suffix
items.text: The usual suffix for all these files is .3g2.

items.title: Brands
items.text: The compatible brands list must contain a brand defined in a 3GPP2 standard.

items.title: Magic number
items.text: None, but the file-type box must occur first in the file.

items.title: Codecs parameter
items.text: Optional, but it must list all codecs of any contained container formats.

items.title: File extensions
items.text: 3g2 and 3gpp2 are both declared, and 3g2 is preferred.
